title: No-match search shows 'No work orders match your filters' in every display
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 15 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [Tech-A], [Tech-B] and [Tech-C]: three eligible technicians at this location. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 No Match" (used by this case only) with three Approved work orders: [WO-1] led by [Tech-A], [WO-2] led by [Tech-B], [WO-3] with no lead.
  • Names and numbers are examples; what must hold: there are work orders in List, Tech View and Board View before the search, and no work order contains the text ZZNOMATCH123.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Create everything below in this location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard), [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards), [Tech-C] (e.g. Jenny Wilson).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 No Match" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 No Match": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
    • [WO-2] (e.g. S1-691): Lead Technician = [Tech-B].
    • [WO-3] (e.g. S1-352): no lead (Lead Technician left empty).
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 No Match" shows [WO-1] (lead [Tech-A]), [WO-2] (lead [Tech-B]) and [WO-3] (no lead). If not, fix the leads before starting, then clear the search.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. In List, click Search and type text no work order contains: ZZNOMATCH123.
  4. Read the message and buttons in the work orders area.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  6. Read the message and buttons.
  7. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  8. Read the message and buttons.
  9. Click Clear filters.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • List, Tech View and Board View each show the message "No work orders match your filters" with a Clear filters action.
  • Tech View and Board View show that one message for the whole page, not a list of empty technician groups or columns.
  • Clicking Clear filters removes the search and the work orders come back.
  • The design shows "No work orders match these filters" and "Clear all filters": that wording is a fail against the specification, write down what you see.

What you should see today (build v26.40.8-7a95011, 10/8/2026): List, Tech View and Board View show "No work orders match these filters", "Try removing a filter to widen your results." and a "Clear all filters" button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark the case Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it reads "No work orders match your filters" with "Clear filters" as described above, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-N1, read 8 Oct 2026. Tech plan revised 24 Sep 2026 (uploaded 8 Oct 2026), section 6 Phase 8. PRD section 9 User Feedback Summary.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-N1: “When filters return no results, show the existing List empty state and Clear filters action in every display: “No work orders match your filters”.”
  • Tech plan 6 Phase 8: “a filter matching nothing shows the shared empty state rather than a screen of empty groups (S1-N1)”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.
